description: The iteration-4 patch to REQ-204 correctly fixes the ONE specific gap FIND-201 raised (the 'economy/gig' bullet's 'the highest-leverage move is to POST' phrase, runtime/loop/prompt.mjs:71, is now named + covered), but it does not close the underlying structural pattern FIND-201 was really about, and a fresh, full re-read of the CURRENT runtime/loop/prompt.mjs turns up a second, still-uncovered instance of the exact same pattern. behavioral-spec.md's REQ-204 now contains THREE textually different scope statements for what is presented as a single, self-consistent criterion: (1) the named-minimum-phrases list ('## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★' block's imperative language, 'Prefer this over re-yielding surplus', 'it is almost never yield again', 'the highest-leverage move is to POST'); (2) the newly-added 'GENERALIZED, BINDING criterion' (Acceptance Criteria bullet 2), whose scope is explicitly defined as 'anywhere within the ## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★ block itself, or anywhere within any paragraph that block references or duplicates'; and (3) Acceptance Criteria bullet 3 (mirrored by PROP-203b in verification-architecture.md), whose scope is 'anywhere in the file's binding (non-tips, non-advice) sections' -- i.e. the WHOLE file. Scope (2) is strictly narrower than scope (3): the '## MINDSET: yield is the bank...' heading section (prompt.mjs lines 98-103) is a SIBLING section to '## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★' (lines 89-96) -- the bootstrap block's own text (lines 89-96) never mentions yield or the MINDSET section, so MINDSET is not 'the block itself' and is not a paragraph the block 'references or duplicates.' Yet MINDSET contains, in the SAME heading section as (and one bullet away from) the one phrase REQ-204 DOES name ('it is almost never "yield again"', lines 102-103), a second, un-named, equally-strong ranking/steering phrase: 'You were funded to GROW the balance, not to sit. Re-yielding every wake = failure.' (line 99). This phrase tells the model that using ONE specific remaining slot (yield) 'every wake' equals 'failure' -- textbook steering under REQ-203's own definition ('any steering text that tells the model WHICH of the remaining options to prefer' -- disparaging one option is the same steering mechanism as praising the others). It is not in REQ-204's named-minimum list, and it falls OUTSIDE the literal boundary of the new 'GENERALIZED, BINDING criterion' (scope (2): block-itself-or-what-it-references), even though it IS inside scope (3) (whole file's binding sections) and inside PROP-203b's scope, since MINDSET carries no 'advice, NOT rules' disclaimer (only the later 'Tips from a senior' section is self-labeled non-binding, per REQ-204's own Edge Cases). This reproduces, inside the very patch meant to close it, the exact PROP-203b vs. PROP-204a disagreement risk REQ-204 explicitly says must never happen: a Phase 3 implementation that satisfies REQ-204's named list AND its narrower 'generalized' bullet (2) to the letter -- by removing exactly the four named phrases and treating 'the block + what it references/duplicates' as the full removal scope -- would leave 'Re-yielding every wake = failure' untouched in the shipped file. PROP-204a (verification-architecture.md), whose Tool/Method column is scoped to 'the FULL ## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★ block AND the full text of any paragraph(s) it references or duplicates (e.g. the economy/gig bullet ...)' -- the same narrower framing as REQ-204's bullet 2 -- could report PASS on that code state, while PROP-203b ('no pre-existing steering block of equivalent strength remains in the file's binding sections' -- whole-file scope) would have to report FAIL for the identical file. This is not a hypothetical: the phrase is real, present in the file today, and sits in a section REQ-204 itself already had to reach into (to name the adjacent 'yield again' phrase) without extending its own stated scope definition to cover the rest of that same section.
